_note: The five group amendments moved on 26 February 2026, from Annexes 1 to 5 to the minutes. Costs are £m for 2026/27, 2027/28 and 2028/29, as printed in each annex's Table A (revenue). Capital schemes appear here as their revenue cost: a revenue contribution to capital, or the cost of borrowing, as the annex states it. Savings are negative. Parts can be reused to build your own amendment; each keeps its source.

pl.title: Two amendments: a revenue and capital package, and one-off public health spending
pl.summary: A £2m fund to modernise care homes and day centres, £5.551m of community safety and highways schemes, more gully clearing, bigger members' grants, the young person's travel scheme and £1 disabled fare for a year, two energy posts, a parking permit team and an Olympics bid team, paid for from the extra Revenue Support Grant, more income from County Hall and the Exchange conference centre, and fewer management posts. A second amendment spends £0.920m of the Public Health Grant Reserve once.
pl.s151: makes no appreciable impact on the financial resilience of the Council

con.title: Six grants and funds, with a £5m pothole fund over two years
con.summary: Bring back the public rights of way grant for parish councils, a new war memorial grant, three more utility permit inspectors, more for the Culture and Sport Fund and the County Book Fund, and a £5m pothole fund over two years, paid for from the extra Revenue Support Grant and, in 2028/29, the savings contingency.
con.s151: makes no appreciable impact on the financial resilience of the Council

ld.title: Mental health support, parking enforcement, two bus gates paused, and £8m for roads and pavements
ld.summary: A mental health advocates team, a mental health awareness programme, six more parking enforcement officers, the two Preston bus gates scrapped for two years and reviewed, more responsive gully work, and £8m of road, pavement, crossing and traffic light schemes paid for by borrowing, funded from the extra Revenue Support Grant, the Public Health Grant Reserve and, in 2028/29, the savings contingency.
ld.s151: makes no appreciable impact on the financial resilience of the Council

lab.title: Seed funding for two new schools, a school bus fare cap and a bus gate trial
lab.summary: Borrowing to seed two new schools, removing Preston bus gate fines on a trial basis, a scheme to cap school bus fares at £1.50 return a day, a Fair Work Charter, an ownership hub for democratic businesses, and studies of council land for housing and of bringing adult social care in house, funded from the extra Revenue Support Grant and £1m of the savings contingency.
lab.s151: makes no appreciable impact on the financial resilience of the Council

owl.title: Four more flood risk staff and clearing West Lancashire's pavement backlog
owl.summary: Four more posts in the county flood risk team and £135,000 a year for two years to clear an estimated 45 miles of overgrown pavements in West Lancashire, with the rest of the extra Revenue Support Grant held in the Strategic Contingency.
owl.s151: presents no additional risks to the Council's Budget between 2026/27 and 2028/29
